title_en.v1.title: DIY 6-Foot Tool Storage Cabinet with 18 Shallow Drawers, Plywood Construction and Casters
title_en.v1.reason: The transcript clearly supports the cabinet size, plywood construction, 18 drawers and mobile caster design.

detailed_summary.v3.overview: The video documents a custom workshop storage cabinet designed to replace deep dresser drawers that had become disorganized catch-alls. The creator's main design goal is space utilization: many shallow drawers prevent tools from being stacked on top of one another and make individual tools easier to access. The finished unit is about 6 feet wide by 2 feet deep and uses three sheets of 3/4-inch plywood plus two sheets of 1/2-inch plywood. The build covers breaking down sheet goods, assembling the carcass, sizing drawer openings accurately, constructing 18 drawers in several heights, installing slides, making false fronts, finishing the top, adding pulls and mounting the unit on casters. Several practical woodworking tricks are highlighted, including using spacers for repeatable carcass dimensions, using two sliding scraps and a clamp to capture exact drawer width instead of relying only on arithmetic, cutting rabbets for thicker drawer bottoms, checking drawers for square, and using paint-stick pieces to maintain consistent 1/8-inch gaps between false fronts. The finished cabinet provides more usable tool-storage space than the previous deep-drawer system and remains movable around the workshop.

sections.heading: Design and material planning
sections.summary: The creator plans a roughly 6-by-2-foot unit from three sheets of 3/4-inch plywood and two sheets of 1/2-inch plywood. Precision matters because nearly all offcuts are intended for later drawer components.

sections.heading: Building the carcass
sections.summary: Vertical sides are cut to 31.5 by 23.5 inches, notched for the toe kick and upper support, then joined with horizontal and rear supports using pocket-hole construction and repeatable spacers.

sections.heading: Sizing and assembling 18 drawers
sections.summary: Drawer sides are ripped in three heights—2.5, 4.5 and 6.25 inches—with 20.5-inch sides. The creator waits for the actual 20-inch slides before finalizing drawer width and uses a physical measuring jig to avoid cumulative measurement errors.

sections.heading: Drawer bottoms, fronts and hardware
sections.summary: Half-inch plywood bottoms are set into rabbets for strength and space efficiency. False fronts are cut from one sheet, painted blue and spaced with approximately 1/8-inch gaps. Pull locations are drilled with a jig.

sections.heading: Finishing and mobility
sections.summary: The top is edge-banded with birch and receives four coats of polyurethane. Casters make the cabinet movable, and the completed shallow-drawer layout provides substantially more organized storage.

practical_details: Approximate finished footprint: 6 ft by 2 ft.
Primary sheet goods: three 3/4-inch plywood sheets and two 1/2-inch plywood sheets.
Drawer side heights: 2.5, 4.5 and 6.25 inches; drawer-side length about 20.5 inches.
The build uses 20-inch drawer slides and 18 drawers.
Use consistent spacers and repeatedly check for square before installing slides and fronts.
A physical width-transfer jig can reduce errors when fitting drawers to real-world slide dimensions.
limitations: The transcript does not provide a complete cut list for every part.
Material costs and specific hardware availability will vary.
The creator notes some materials are heavier or more robust than necessary, so builders may choose lighter drawer construction.

editorial_assessment.v1.chatgpt_take: A strong, practical workshop build with useful repeatability tricks and concrete dimensions. It is especially valuable for anyone trying to avoid deep drawers that waste vertical space.
editorial_assessment.v1.bottom_line: Keep it as a high-value woodworking reference for shallow-drawer tool storage and drawer-fitting techniques.
